localBiteReport: The week of September 4–8, 2026 is showing the first real signs of the fall transition on Choctawhatchee Bay, with water at 88°F and bait schools on the move. Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters) reports that greenies are pushing out of deeper open water and into the bayous, bridge areas, and flats, which is drawing more consistent action near structure. Redfish opportunities are improving for sight fishing on the flats, and early-morning timing is key as the heat continues to shut things down mid-day. The report does not specifically call out a strong speckled trout, flounder, or black drum bite this week — the dominant inshore story right now is redfish on the flats as fall patterns begin to develop.
